handoff: review#2: fix addresses the cause; review#1 points addressed; typecheck + 1213 tests green. Blocking F1: runCheckOrder releases the lease by substring-matching run_id in raw unvalidated lease JSON (AGENTS: every JSON read validated) — add a store helper that reads the lease validated and releases only on matching run_id. Minor: replaceIfUnchanged gap (F2), null identify releases a live child's lease (F3), duplicated check-running predicate core/view (F4), no tests for parallel checks/K3 rerun (F5), heartbeat-item attribution fallback untouched (F6). Nits F7-F9.

findings.title: Lease ownership is decided by substring-matching raw, unvalidated lease JSON
findings.detail:
The finally block of runCheckOrder runs `readText(join(leasesDir(order.home), order.lease_file))?.includes(`"${order.run_id}"`)`. AGENTS.md Rules (S1/S2) say: 'Every JSON read is validated against @norn/schema'. This read is also cli reaching into the store's lease layout (leasesDir + raw text) instead of going through a store helper.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Add a store helper, e.g. `releaseLeaseOf(home, file, run_id)`. It reads with readJsonFile('lease', …), releases only when lease.run_id matches (ideally with removeIfUnchanged on the raw read), and returns whether it released. Call it here. Cover it with a test in leases-lock.test.ts: a reclaimed lease with another run_id stays.

findings.title: replaceIfUnchanged leaves a gap where the lease file is absent
findings.detail:
The function renames path → aside, then next → path. In between, `check-N.json` does not exist. Another repo's tick on the same machine (~/.norn is shared) can createExclusive the same slot in that gap. The final renameSync then overwrites that lease silently, and a sweep in that gap does not see this run's lease. The window is microseconds.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Finish with linkSync(next, path), which fails with EEXIST and returns false (then unlink next), instead of renameSync. Or document the window next to F4's.

findings.title: A null identify(pid) for a live child releases the lease
findings.detail:
`if (!holder) releaseLease(...)` treats any null from identify as 'already gone'. A failed ps probe also returns null while `norn check-run` is still running. The next tick then sees no lease and no receipt and starts the same check again. identify throwing takes the catch path: it unlinks the order and releases the lease while the child may still run.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Before releasing, check with process liveness (kill 0) that the pid is really gone. If it is alive but unidentified, keep the tick's lease and log.

findings.title: The 'check running' predicate is duplicated in core and view
findings.detail:
items.ts uses `step?.type === "check" && uf.lease?.kind === "check"`. load.ts uses the same test plus `!!st && !st.park`. The two can drift (Duplicated Code).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Add one exported predicate in core (e.g. `checkRunning(step, uf, st)`) and use it in both places.

findings.title: Parallel checks, claim renewal and the K3 rerun of a dead check-run are not tested
findings.detail:
The spec says 'Checks up to `max_checks` actually run in parallel' and 'claims keep being renewed'. The act/check.ts header says a dead check-run's lease is reclaimed and the check reruns. No test starts two checks in one tick, advances past a claim renewal while a check runs, or kills a check-run.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add a test where one tick starts two checks and both orders or leases are live at once. Optionally add one that kills the check-run pid and expects run_check again.

findings.title: The 'no heartbeat' item still attaches to the first held story
findings.detail:
Wanted, 'Until then, at minimum: … attached to a story that needs the heartbeat … rather than to the first held story.' This is a fallback, and the main fix makes it far rarer. Still, heartbeatItem still uses `facts.stories.find((s) => s.claim.state === "mine")`, so the gh-61 case remains when watch is really down.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Leave it out of this fix and have the person file it as its own issue, or pick a held auto story with live units.

findings.title: slice(0, -3) depends on group order
findings.detail:
The 'Other' group is inserted before the last three groups because those are the non-person ones. Adding a group breaks this silently.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Split HELP_GROUPS by `for === "person"`.

findings.title: sweepCheckOrders builds a set that contains false and null
findings.detail:
`.map((e) => e.lease.kind === "check" && e.lease.run_id)` adds false and null values to a set of run ids. It works only by accident.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Filter first, then map.

findings.title: The comment overstates what stays off disk
findings.detail:
The comment says 'secrets in it never reach the disk'. That holds only for the process env: `.env.norn` and the action env are still written into the order (mode 0600).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Reword: 'the process env is inherited, not written; the order holds only .env.norn, the step env and NORN_HOME'.
